--- daily-logger is the automated pipeline that generates, reviews, and publishes these daily development articles — it runs on a schedule, proposes and verifies suggested actions via a two-agent CI loop, and writes output to the article UI. Sunday's six commits all landed there: article generation, independent accuracy review, action-registry landing and its recovery record, editorial acceptance of the corrected October 18 article, and YAML workflow repair. The prompt-size concern in issue #386 remains real: the action-review pipeline assembles source material — held suggestions, identity records, rejection history — into complete prompts for two agents (a proposer and a verifier). The CI fixed-context probe measured 274,352 proposer bytes and 274,321 verifier bytes, both below its 327,680-byte (320 KiB) probe guard. Runtime evidence limits are 131,072 bytes (128 KiB) per source and 393,216 bytes (384 KiB) in total; source rejection stops before either action-agent call. Each complete prompt has its own 655,360-byte (640 KiB) guard before its corresponding call, so verifier-prompt overflow could occur after a proposer invocation. These are byte checks, not token-window or output-reserve qualification. During Monday October 19's initial generation run (reporting Sunday's activity), the action review recorded a generic source-budget rejection — the assembled source material exceeded a runtime evidence limit and the review fell back to a pending state. The exact source packet from that original run was not retained. The #385 clustered-timestamp popover fix has a reviewed preview awaiting the human's visual acceptance and explicit merge decision. ## What shipped ### daily-logger ([#388](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/388)) Repaired the daily blog workflow YAML by combining duplicate top-level `env` mappings into one ([#388](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/388)). The duplicate header caused strict js-yaml parsing to fail at line 39:1, blocking that scheduled generator. The repair is a separately verified two-line change (deleting the redundant `env:` header and its blank line) on the accepted #387 base; all three environment values and every other parsed workflow field are unchanged. - `db69911` ### daily-logger ([#387](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/387), [#384](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/384)) Accepted the corrected October 18 article and reconciled its suggested actions ([#387](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/387)), superseding draft correction PR [#384](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/384) (closed without merge). Draft #384 was superseded because the intervening merge of #381 changed canonical policy and trusted-ancestor requirements, creating a boundary that the original branch could not cleanly cross; #387 was an explicitly authorized source and data bootstrap against the new base. The branch, workflow run, and correspondence history from [#384](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/384) are preserved as auditable evidence of the review cycle. The human reviewer explicitly authorized acceptance after independent review. - `f94b11a` ### daily-logger ([#381](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/381)) Merged the verified action registry reconciliation for article suggestions ([#381](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/381)). The action registry is the provenance ledger that tracks AI-generated suggested actions across the pipeline's two-agent loop (a proposer agent and a separate verifier agent). It deduplicates identities, enforces evidence requirements, and maintains a record of what was proposed, verified, and accepted or deferred. New identities are capped at two per article lifecycle and require factual evidence, goal evidence, and an independent verifier. The 138 historical suggestions are preserved as unadmitted records used for duplicate detection and rejection memory; they predate the current admission policy and have not passed its checks. - `4108758` ### daily-logger ([#383](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/383)) Registered the independent accuracy review of the October 18 draft as a source-pinned record visible in the article UI ([#383](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/383)). Ten confirmed findings and two unverified claim groups; all dispositions remained open at merge time. - `aa6dc7b` ### daily-logger Recorded the action-registry landing recovery. GitHub rejected the existing integrated history as non-rebaseable. The tested history was saved, and a linear commit with an identical tree was prepared on the accepted aa6dc7b base. The record preserves how this landing was recovered. - `c88039f` ### daily-logger ([#382](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/382)) Generated and committed the 2026-10-18 article via the daily blog bot ([#382](https://github.com/ojfbot/daily-logger/pull/382)). - `d540e2c` ## The decisions ### Combining duplicate workflow `env` blocks rather than adding a third — *tooling-for-iteration* The YAML repair deleted the redundant `env:` header and its blank line rather than patching around the duplicate or restructuring the file. Strict js-yaml parsing rejects files with two top-level keys of the same name at the first duplicate occurrence — adding `ACTION_REVIEW_DISABLED` to the existing mapping is the structurally correct fix and leaves no surface for future writers to misread the file as intentionally split. Tags: `ci-cd`, `hardening` ### Closing PR #384 without merge and superseding via PR #387 — *model-behavior-as-design* Draft correction #384 was closed without merge after the intervening merge of #381 changed canonical policy and trusted-ancestor requirements, creating a boundary the original branch could not cleanly cross. PR #387 was opened as an explicitly authorized source and data bootstrap against the new base, after independent verification and human authorization. Closing #384 without merge preserves the branch, workflow run, and correspondence history as auditable evidence of the review cycle while ensuring only a fully verified candidate lands on main. Tags: `editorial-pipeline`, `provenance`, `assistant-centric` ### Capping new action identities at two per article lifecycle with evidence requirements — *model-behavior-as-design* The verified action registry introduced in #381 caps new suggestion identities at two per article lifecycle and requires factual evidence, goal evidence, and an independent verifier for each. Without this cap the registry grows unboundedly with every article pass, making duplicate detection unreliable and prompt-size management harder to bound. The tradeoff is real but bounded: legitimate suggestions beyond the cap are held, not dropped. The 138 historical suggestions are preserved as unadmitted records serving duplicate detection and rejection memory; they predate the current admission policy and have not passed its checks. Note: on Monday, after this review, daily-logger #391 was separately adopted and merged (at `730fb9f`) — it repairs bounded whole-source selection and applies the user's prospective initial 3–5 target / at-most-two NEW per deliberately requested revision policy. That is Monday follow-through, not Sunday-shipped behavior; the historical two-new-identities lifecycle ceiling describes Sunday's source version. Tags: `editorial-pipeline`, `provenance`, `model-behavior-as-design` ### Recording the action-registry landing recovery — *tooling-for-iteration* GitHub rejected the existing integrated history of the action-registry PR #381 as non-rebaseable. The tested history was saved, and a linear commit with an identical tree was prepared on the accepted aa6dc7b base. The c88039f record preserves how this landing was recovered. Tags: `ci-cd`, `hardening`, `provenance` ## Roadmap pulse **Token-budget scoping (daily-logger #386) — open.** The action-review pipeline runs two agents — a proposer and a verifier — each currently receiving assembled source material checked against runtime evidence limits (131,072 bytes per source, 393,216 bytes total) before either action-agent call. Each complete prompt has its own 655,360-byte guard before its corresponding model call. The CI fixed-context probe measured 274,352 proposer bytes and 274,321 verifier bytes, both below its 327,680-byte probe guard. During Monday October 19's initial generation (reporting Sunday's activity), the source-budget check recorded a generic rejection and the review fell back to a pending state; the exact source packet from that original run was not retained. On Monday, daily-logger #391 delivered bounded whole-source selection (merged at `730fb9f`), repairing the source-budget overflow; #391 additionally checks the complete serialized provider request, including system and tools. Bounded whole-source selection is Monday follow-through, not proof that token qualification or all future source-capacity cases are solved. The tokenizer/model-window/output-reserve qualification and suggestion quality improvements under #386 remain open work. **daily-logger #385** (OPEN DRAFT) — `fix: use existing map popovers for clustered PR timestamps`. Clustered timestamp ranges such as `~19:28–19:42Z` need to open the existing timezone-offset/day-night-map popover individually per clock. This is the remaining UI gap after the local-time world map popover feature shipped in #372. The PR has a reviewed preview awaiting the human's visual acceptance and explicit merge decision. It is bounded to a single-article pilot; wider follow-up has separate limits. It is not blocking any other open item. **lego-village-pipeline #46, #45, #44** (OPEN DRAFT) — Three design-review PRs. Drafts #44 and #46 specify close-or-supersede exits rather than merge, with operative import/reconstruction criteria. Draft #45 has the distinct HOUSE-WORLD R0/HANDOFF-037 record, a second-steward check, and James's merge control. The source-pinned pickup guide already assigns Grid/Subgrid, navigation/state, and motion follow-ups to their respective owners. Each record has a documented exit and owner gate. *Editorial recommendation (subject to existing owners):* if these remain open past the next weekly update without a disposition change, they could be explicitly parked. **core #540** — `Refine the skills-and-knowledge value pilot before execution`. This is a follow-up to the Paperthin skills pilot — a separate workstream evaluating how well the assistant applies retained knowledge to real work items, unrelated to the daily-logger pipeline. Operator agreed to continue tuning; no execution is authorized. Next action: select a real work item, revise the comparison protocol, return for owner review. **core #307** — `Wayfinder map — fleet-runner`. The existing map lists nine inherited questions and the #315 census / #308 scheduled-agent research frontier as documented preparatory work. Authority, consumption, reach, recovery, and S25 reconciliation decisions remain open owner gates. Runtime implementation remains gated; documented census, research and decision preparation can continue. ## What's next **Priority 1 — Token-budget qualification under daily-logger #386.** The bounded whole-source selection repair shipped Monday in #391 (at `730fb9f`), resolving the source-budget overflow observed during Monday's initial generation. Remaining open work: tokenizer/model-window/output-reserve qualification and suggestion quality under the revised source selection. Bounded whole-source selection is delivered Monday follow-through, not Sunday-shipped behavior and not proof that token qualification or all future source-capacity cases are solved. Do not re-implement the already-delivered bounded source repair as new work. **Priority 2 — Move daily-logger #385 through visual acceptance.** The clustered PR timestamp popover fix has a reviewed preview awaiting the human's visual acceptance and explicit merge decision. It is bounded to a single-article pilot; wider follow-up has separate limits. It is listed second because it is not blocking anything. > **Suggested actions**
